INDEPENDENT REVIEW 5 OF 1.24.40'S PDF TOOLS -- 2026-11-26
Build under review: lantern_1240_r5.html (1.24.40, frozen copy, sha256 15d38844dbb195cc...), served as index.html in
Playwright's Chromium. Compared with lantern_1240_r4.html (sha256 7ce86d325a43bf93..., one round of mends earlier) and
old_1239_index.html (1.24.39). I did not see this code being written and changed nothing outside this folder. Line
numbers are of the frozen r5 file.

RESULT: 1855 checks, 100 failed (cases.json, cases.log; `python3 run_review.py <new.html> <old.html> [groups]` from this
folder; env CJNAME, R3OUT, R3EV honoured).
  hyph 1574 / 45   ls 54 / 13   enc 70 / 30   kept 8 / 4   links 21 / 0   forms 21 / 2   deep 32 / 3   flat 15 / 0
  sweep 60 / 3
Of the 100: 6 are my oracle's or fixture's fault (listed at the end); the rest are the findings below.

HOW IT WAS TRIED (make_fixtures.py; all made by programs that are not Lantern)
  reportlab  hy_rl.pdf (6 pages, Helvetica 10, lines drawn one run each): two columns / full-width heading / two columns;
             two columns over a table; two columns over a rule and a footnote; dash-bulleted and numbered lists with
             hanging indents, five first-line-indented paragraphs, a hanging-indent paragraph, a list of prefixes
             ("anti-", "counter-", ...); right-aligned and centred lines; a table of narrow cells wrapping inside the cell;
             a right column starting 30 pt lower and shorter than the left. ls_rl2.pdf: chess files a-h centred in 14 pt
             squares, Y N Y N Y cells at a 12 pt pitch, QWERTY keys centred at 16 pt, KIRKSTALL drawn a letter at a time
             0.4 em apart in Helvetica and in Courier.
  Chromium   hy_chrome.pdf: 225 made-up names (Thorn-den-field ...) with &shy; between syllables, each used once, packed so
             most lines end in a break: CSS two columns (justified and not), a full-width h2, a picture box, a table and
             a footnote under columns, ul/ol, text-indent, hanging indent, right and centred blocks, narrow table cells,
             three columns. ls_chrome2.pdf: 19 lines of single letters and letter-spacing (see finding 6-9).
  LibreOffice lo_word.pdf: a .docx made by python-docx and set by soffice: header and footer, a one-column heading and
             paragraphs, then a continuous two-column section, then List Bullet / List Number, first-line and hanging
             indents, right and centred paragraphs; 190 made-up names with U+00AD, each once.
  pikepdf    enc_std.pdf (13 pages, one font each, no /Widths): Helvetica, Times-Roman, Courier, Helvetica-Bold,
             Times-BoldItalic, Arial, TimesNewRoman with no /Encoding; Helvetica with /Differences and no /BaseEncoding;
             WinAnsi; MacRoman; Symbol; ZapfDingbats; Helvetica with /Encoding /StandardEncoding. Codes 0x27 0x60 0xAE
             0xAF 0xE8 0xE1 0xFB 0xF9 0xB1 0xAA 0xBA 0xA4. links2.pdf: a /Names /Dests tree with /Kids and /Limits, the
             word in two names; catalog /Dests with /OrmskirkTown; links by /Dest string, /A GoTo, /Dest name, GoToR to
             "Ormskirk-annex.pdf"; bookmarks by each means. forms2.pdf: fields on two pages, only page 1 marked: a text
             field with a widget on each page under one parent, radio groups with a button on each page (selected on one
             or the other), a parent with a child on each page, a check box on page 2. forms3.pdf: the word only where no
             page shows it (see 12). deep256/deep257/deep_unmarked(200)/deep_unmarked70.pdf: forms nested 1, 100, 200,
             255, 256, 257 deep on the marked page, or 70 / 200 deep on an unmarked page; a form that draws itself.
             noap.pdf: no appearances, /NeedAppearances: check boxes with /MK /CA 8 4 l n u H and none, one Off; radios
             with no /CA and with u; a multi-select list box (Banana, Damson chosen); a comb field (MaxLen 8, AB12CD).
  reportlab  kept.pdf (DejaVu Sans embedded): Latin with precomposed and combining accents, Greek, Cyrillic, fi fl ffl,
             Turkish I-dot; lines turned 90, -90, 30 degrees, and slanted; "Ormskirk" first on each.
Oracles: poppler 24.02 (pdftotext -bbox, -bbox-layout, -layout, pdfinfo -dests, pdftoppm), pdfminer/pdfplumber (letters,
fonts), pypdf 6.17 (text, fields), pikepdf/qpdf (NameTree lookup by /Limits, outline, widgets, --check, --qdf), each
fixture's design. The runner imports review 3's r3lib.py (unchanged). Scratch copies go to the scratchpad's r5out.

FINDINGS
1. [L] A word broken at the foot of a column is joined to whatever full-width thing stands just under that column (a
   heading, a table's first row, a footnote), and the real second half at the head of the next column is not found.
   Smallest: hy_rl.pdf p1: "Winter-" ends column 1 (231,667); the heading "Results of the survey..." starts at x 72, 22
   pt under it; "bourne" heads column 2 (312,758). Search "Winterbourne": 0 places; "WinterResults": 1. p2: "Kirk-" over
   a table whose first cell "Valve" is 20 pt under it: "Kirkstall" 0, "KirkValve" 1. p3: "Feather-" over a footnote
   "1 See the annual report..." 20 pt under it: "Featherstonehaugh" 0, "Feather1" 1. LibreOffice (lo_word.pdf p1): "Mar-"
   ends column 1 of the two-column section over the heading "Lists and indents": "MarLists" 1 (poppler's own order puts
   the heading next, so my oracle could not place "Mardenholm"; see the end).
   Evidence: redacting ["Winterbourne", "Kirkstall", "Featherstonehaugh", ...] leaves "Winter-", "bourne", "Kirk-",
   "stall", "Feather-", "stonehaugh" in poppler's words of the copy. evidence/1_hy_rl_p1_wrong_joins.png (red: the
   WinterResults and Pemberbourne marks; blue: Thornton, found; no mark for Winterbourne). r4 the same.
   Traced (marksOf, under() ~line 53318): the first line within 2.5 sizes under the word that has a run between the
   column's edge and the word is taken, whatever it is; anyUnder() then keeps the foot-of-column path from running.
   Direction: a line under the word goes on its column only if it is one of the column's own lines: about the same size,
   at the column's own line pitch (not a gap of 1.5 pitches or more), and not running past the next column's edge (a
   full-width heading, footnote or table row does). Otherwise treat the word as at the column's foot.

2. [L] The foot of a column in the lower of two two-column sections goes on at the head of the next column of the
   UPPER section.
   Smallest: hy_rl.pdf p1: "Pember-" ends column 1 of the lower section (219,528); "ton" heads its column 2 (312,706).
   Search "Pemberton": 0; "Pemberbourne": 1 (joined to "bourne" at the top of the page). Chromium (hy_chrome.pdf p1):
   "Pen-ing-" ends column 1 of the section above the picture box, "worth" heads its column 2 at (317,626): "Peningworth"
   0. "Pemberbourne" is new in r5 (r4 found neither).
   Traced (the foot path after anyUnder, ~line 53361): the top-most line of the whole page with a run at the next edge.
   Direction: take the top-most line at the next edge that is under the nearest full-width line (or the top of the
   word's own run of column lines) above the word, i.e. the head of the same section's next column.

3. [L][R] A column whose lines start fewer than 40% as often as at the page's busiest edge is not taken as a column, and
   a word broken in it is joined to the line under it in the column to its left.
   Smallest: lo_word.pdf p1 (Word-style document set by LibreOffice): a one-column heading and paragraphs, then a
   two-column section. Lines start a run at x 90 34 times and at x 315 (column 2) 12 times; 0.4 x 34 = 13.6 > 12, so 315
   is not in `strong`. "Langber-" ends a column-2 line (485-522, y 504.5), "holm" starts the next column-2 line at 315.
   Search "Langberholm": 0; "Langberley": 1 (joined to column 1's "ley" at x 90). The same for Ingleygate, Kelbershaw,
   Kelwickbeck and Fenbygarth: 5 of the 6 breaks in column 2 of that page. r4 found all five. With only the lines from
   y 200 to 600 handed to redactMarks, "Langberholm" is found (so it is the count). evidence/2_lo_word_col2_joined_to_col1.png
   (green: the Langberley mark).
   Traced (~line 53283): strong = clusters with n >= max(3, 0.4 x nMax). Then cand = [90, ...]; under(90) finds the next
   line's first run at 90 and returns (pairing "langber"+"ley" fails the search, but the loop has already returned).
   Direction: judge an edge against the lines at its own heights (the lines whose y-range it shares), not the page's
   busiest edge; and let a run that itself starts after a column-wide gap on the word's own line count as an edge
   (the "Lang" line starts a run at 315 after an 18 pt gap).

4. [R] Centred text broken at a hyphen is no longer found.
   Smallest: hy_rl.pdf p5, centred on x 297: "Notes on the heat engine and its Thermo-" / "dynamics as taught at the
   works school": r4 finds "Thermodynamics", r5 finds nothing. (Right-aligned "...has an Electro-" / "magnetic flow
   meter..." is found by neither; the hanging-indent paragraph's first line "...Lindis-" (x 72) / "farne" (x 108) by
   neither.) Not traced beyond: no candidate edge has the next line starting at it (the lines' own starts are not edges),
   and anyUnder() stops the rest. Direction: where the word's line starts at no edge (centred or right-aligned text), or
   the next line starts at a hanging indent, take the line just under it (one pitch, same size) whose extent overlaps
   it.

5. [O] Lines that each hold one prefix are joined: hy_rl.pdf p4 "anti-" / "counter-" / "de-" / "inter-" (a list, one
   per line, x 72): "anticounter", "counterde", "deinter" are found. The rule's "short line followed by small letters is a
   break" reads a glossary list as broken words. Low (only a search for the joined string is affected). r4 the same.

6. [L][R] Letter-spacing in a monospaced font is no longer read as words.
   Smallest: ls_chrome2.pdf, `<p style="letter-spacing:.3em;font-family:monospace">SOWERBY BRIDGE</p>`: r5 reads
   "S O W E R B Y B R I D G E" and search "SOWERBY" finds nothing; r4 read "SOWERBY BRIDGE". ls_rl2.pdf, KIRKSTALL drawn a
   letter at a time in Courier 12 with 0.4 em gaps: r5 "K I R K S T A L L", r4 "KIRKSTALL" (the Helvetica line is read).
   Traced (~line 49381): "ssp > gsp + 0.01 x size": in a monospaced font every letter has the same width, so the starts
   are exactly as even as the gaps. Direction: when the row's letters all have one advance, decide by the gap itself
   (letter-spacing leaves a gap under the font's space advance plus the spacing that a word gap would have); or only
   use the starts test for proportional fonts.

7. [L] A letter-spaced word inside a sentence is not read (r4 and 1.24.39 the same).
   Smallest: ls_chrome2.pdf `<p>Site: <span style="letter-spacing:.3em">KIRKSTALL</span> today</p>` -> "Site: K I R K S
   T A L L today"; search "KIRKSTALL": 0, so Redact cannot take it out. (Letter-spaced emphasis inside running text is
   ordinary in German typesetting.)
   Traced: Chromium draws the plain word after the span a letter at a time too, so the row of single letters is
   K I R K S T A L L t o d a y; its smallest gaps (0) are inside "today", and fewer than 6 in 10 gaps are near them.
   Direction: split a row of single letters where the gap jumps (over the space advance, or over twice the median)
   before testing evenness, and test each piece on its own.

8. [L] One kerned pair in a letter-spaced line breaks another word (r4 the same).
   Smallest: ls_chrome2.pdf, letter-spacing .3em, DejaVu Sans 11: "SAFETY FIRST AT ALL TIMES" -> "S AFETY FIRST AT ALL
   TIMES"; search "SAFETY": 0. Gaps 3.30 pt, the kerned "AT"/"TA" 2.45, the gap after "S" 3.50; the tolerance is taken
   from the smallest gap (2.45 + 0.08 x 11 = 3.33), so 3.50 is a space. Direction: take the tolerance about the median
   (or most common) gap, not the smallest.

9. [O][R] Single letters with plain spaces are still joined when nothing else is on their line (1.24.39 read them apart).
   Smallest: ls_chrome2.pdf, no CSS: "A B C D" -> "ABCD"; "• A B C D" (a bullet) -> "•ABCD"; "Q W E R T Y" -> "QWERTY";
   "I V X L C D M"; "K Q R B N P"; and with letter-spacing .3em, "A B C D" (spaces in the text) -> "ABCD". poppler and
   1.24.39 read them apart (r4 joined them too). Every gap here is 3.49 pt = DejaVu Sans' space advance (0.318 em x 11).
   ls_rl2.pdf: chess files a-h centred in 14 pt squares (Helvetica 9) -> "abcde f gh" (1.24.39 "a b c d e f g h").
   A Redact of one letter then blacks out the whole joined row. Passing now: "A B C D E" in serif and monospace, the
   Y N Y N Y cells, QWERTY keys at 16 pt, "Grades:"-style lines (r4's finding).
   Direction (as review 4 said): a gap within ~0.05 em of the font's space advance is a word space; and a row of
   centred letters at an even pitch has even centres, which a letter-spaced word never has.

10. [D][L] StandardEncoding is used only for a standard font with no /Encoding at all.
   a. [L] /Encoding /StandardEncoding named outright is read as Windows': enc_std.pdf p13 (Helvetica): "the ®nance of the
      ¯uent pump", "èukasz and ásir at the Straûe by the ùre", "pages 1±2 and ªHelloº and 1¤2 inch"; poppler and the
      table: "finance", "fluent", "Łukasz", "Æsir", "Straße", "øre", "1–2", "“Hello”", "1⁄2". Search "finance" finds
      nothing there, so Redact leaves it. (font(), ~line 49155: baseEnc "/StandardEncoding" falls to WIN[c].)
   b. [D] /Encoding << /Differences [65 /Aring] >> with no /BaseEncoding on Helvetica: the codes not in /Differences are
      the font's built-in StandardEncoding (ISO 32000-1 9.6.6.1); Lantern reads them as WinAnsi (p8). poppler and
      pdfminer read StandardEncoding.
   c. [D] Non-embedded "Arial" and "TimesNewRoman" with no /Encoding: poppler and pdfminer read StandardEncoding,
      Lantern WinAnsi (p6, p7); the rule's name test (/^(Helvetica|Times|Courier)(-|,|$)/) leaves them out.
   d. [D] StandardEncoding letters outside Windows' set are measured by the browser's font, not Adobe's widths: Helvetica
      "pages 1–2 and “Hello” and 1⁄2 inch" ends at 262.1 against poppler's 257.4 (fraction: Adobe 167/1000, Lantern
      about 556); lines with Ł and ⁄ in Times-Roman, Helvetica-Bold, Times-BoldItalic are 1.3-5.4 pt off. The
      Times-BoldItalic line was within 1 pt in r4 (minor regression).
   e. [D] (outside the rule, as in r4) /MacRomanEncoding codes above 127 are read as nothing: p10 "the nance of the uent
      pump", "Strae"; poppler reads Æ, Ø, ß... (font().uni: `baseEnc === "/MacRomanEncoding" && c > 127` returns "").
   Unaffected and right: Helvetica, Times-Roman, Courier, Helvetica-Bold, Times-BoldItalic with no /Encoding (text equal to
   poppler, pdfminer and Adobe's table; 0x27 ’, 0x60 ‘, 0xAE fi, 0xAF fl); WinAnsi; Symbol; ZapfDingbats.

11. [D] Kept words in a redacted copy (kept.pdf, "Ormskirk" redacted on every line).
   a. A word after the redacted one on a 30-degree line is drawn but no longer written as text: "Ormskirk Penrith Keswick"
      turned 30 degrees; in the copy poppler, pypdf and pdfplumber find no "Penrith" (pdfplumber's letters of the copy
      run "...Keswick" with no Penrith), while the picture still shows it (evidence/3_kept_turned_penrith.png, original
      left, copy right). The level, 90 and -90 and slanted lines keep every word.
   b. pdfminer reads kept words split where a letter's stretch is wrong: "naï ve" (the copy writes ï with a horizontal
      scale of 0.4997 against 1.1 for its neighbours: `0.4997 0 0 1 176.41 720 Tm <ef> Tj`, as if ï were twice as wide),
      Αθήνα, κόσμος, Μόσχα, Москва, журнал, Щётка as single letters, "baffl e" (U+FB04), "i stanbul" (İ). pdfminer read
      them whole in the original; poppler and pypdf read them whole in the copy. Direction: take each letter's width
      from the same table the copy's font declares (/Widths of the invisible font), including ï, İ, the ligatures and
      the non-Latin letters.

12. [L] Redact with words leaves the word in form fields that no marked page shows (r4 the same).
   Smallest: forms3.pdf: page 1 says "Ormskirk" (marked); page 2 (not marked) has a check box named "ormskirk_resident",
   a field whose tooltip /TU is "Ormskirk residents only", a hidden widget (/F 6) whose value is "Ormskirk Road" (its
   appearance stream draws it), and an orphan field (no widget) "hidden_town" = "Ormskirk". The copy keeps all four:
   qpdf --qdf shows /T (ormskirk_resident), /TU (Ormskirk residents only), /V (Ormskirk Road), /V (Ormskirk) and
   "(Ormskirk Road) Tj"; pypdf reads the three fields with them. Direction: with words, scrub every field's /T, /TU,
   /TM, /V, /DV, /Opt and appearance streams across the form, as the bookmarks and named places are (rename, put out the
   word, or drop the field and its widgets).

13. [D] An unmarked page's forms nested more than 66 deep are cut in the copy (r4 the same).
   Smallest: deep_unmarked70.pdf: page 2 (no word) draws "Dalegarth" through 70 nested forms; poppler reads it in the
   original. In the copy the 67th form is a bare stream with no /Type or /Subtype (poppler: "XObject subtype is missing
   or wrong type") and Dalegarth is gone; the 200-deep page likewise stops at 67. Redact gave no message (its 256 test
   looks only at marked pages).
   Traced: builder().copy (line ~51496) returns null past depth 200, and each form level is three steps (stream,
   /Resources, /XObject). Direction: copy without a depth cap (iteratively, objects already copied are already
   numbered), or apply the same refusal as for marked pages.

WHAT PASSED
- Rule 1: all 225 Chromium names but one (Peningworth, finding 2), including breaks in ul/ol items, the first line of
  text-indent paragraphs, hanging indents, narrow table cells (Northal-ler-/ton style), three columns and the foot of a
  column with nothing under it; LibreOffice's column 1, lists, indents, right and centred paragraphs (all but the six
  above; its centred "Gardale-"/"royd" is found, which r4 missed); reportlab: Bradford and Thornton inside columns, Raven-/sworth in column 2 over a table, Ulverston (foot of
  column 1, the right column starting 30 pt lower and shorter), Hollingsworth and Ashworth-Bramley in bulleted items,
  Quarmby in a numbered item, Ravens-/worth on the first line of an indented paragraph (r4 missed it), Alnmouth in a
  hanging indent, Hydrostatic and Gearbox in narrow cells. Not joined: "AXMain", "AXLever", "HydroValve", "GearMain",
  "Ulverthe", "Pembernew", "Kirkthe", "Winterthe", "FeatherSee"/"Featherthe". No mark off its word in any found place.
- Rule 2: letter-spacing .15em at 6 pt serif, .3em serif, .5em at 24 pt, .2em at 40 pt, small capitals with spacing;
  "A B C D E" in serif and in monospace with plain spaces; one-letter table cells; H2SO4/NaCl/CO2 with subscripts;
  chess notation "1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6"; Helvetica letters drawn 0.4 em apart; QWERTY keys; Y N Y N Y cells.
- Rule 3: see 10 (the no-/Encoding Helvetica/Times/Courier family is right in text and in fi/fl places).
- Rule 4: poppler and pypdf read every kept word whole and in place except Penrith (11a): accents precomposed and
  combining, Greek, Cyrillic, fi fl ffl, İstanbul, the 90, -90 and slanted lines.
- Rule 5: links2.pdf: pages 1 and 3 marked; qpdf --check clean; the names tree rebuilt sorted with right /Limits (qpdf's
  NameTree finds every name); links on the unmarked page 4 by /Dest string, GoTo /D and /Dest name still go to pages 2,
  3, 3, 4, 2; the GoToR to "Ormskirk-annex.pdf" dropped; pdfinfo -dests names the same pages with no name holding the
  word; the four bookmarks go to the same pages, "Plan of Ormskirk" -> "Plan of ███"; the word nowhere in the bytes.
- Rule 6: forms2.pdf: only page 1's widgets made part of the page (values Alice Weaver, REF-77, 12 Moor Lane shown as
  page text); page 2 keeps every widget with its state; pypdf reads city, ref (the parent with a kid on each page),
  choice and pick (radio groups across the pages), addr.town and agree with their values; /AcroForm kept; qpdf clean.
- Rule 7: forms 1-256 deep on a marked page read and kept in the copy (poppler itself stops near 100 in the original);
  257 deep on the marked page: Redact refuses with the 256 message; a form that draws itself read once.
- Rule 8: noap.pdf flattened: each ticked box drawn as its /MK /CA ZapfDingbats letter (8 4 l n u H) in its box, the box
  with no /CA as '3' (a tick), the Off box nothing, the radios as 'l' and 'u'; the list box shows Apple Banana Cherry
  Damson... with bands behind Banana and Damson only; the comb AB12CD a letter a cell (within 2 pt of each centre);
  qpdf clean.
- Sweep: 57 PDFs under tests/fixtures (the review folders, pdf_open, ...) read by r5 and r4: every page the same text.

FAILED CHECKS THAT ARE MY ORACLE'S OR FIXTURE'S FAULT (6)
- ls "(oracle) poppler reads 'Y N Y N Y'" and "'H2SO4 and NaCl and CO2'": poppler's own reading (cells on lines of their
  own; subscripts apart); a second opinion only, Lantern passes both.
- hyph lo_word.pdf "'Mardenholm' found by poppler (fixture check)": poppler orders the heading after column 1's foot, so
  my joiner (which follows poppler's order) could not place the break; the case is finding 1.
- sweep cert_pubsec.pdf, damaged_lock_no_OU.pdf, damaged_lock_r6_no_UE.pdf "read by both": files that are meant to be
  refused (certificate and damaged locks); both builds refuse them with their messages.
- Partly: kept "poppler puts each kept word where it was" and "poppler reads every kept word..." list fragments of the
  30-degree line ('w', 'es', 'kir', ...) because poppler reads turned text in pieces that differ between original and
  copy; the real loss in them is Penrith (11a).

NOT CHECKED
- Word itself (no Word here: the Word-like document is python-docx set by LibreOffice); footnotes from LibreOffice
  (python-docx cannot make them; footnotes were tried in reportlab and Chromium).
- Writer's or Word's own letter-spacing (review 4 found it outside the rule); xelatex/pdflatex this round.
- An embedded Type 1 font named Helvetica (no Type 1 font file to embed); only the r5-vs-r4 sweep stands for embedded
  fonts being unaffected. 1.24.39 could be compared only on letter-spacing (its pageText has no boxes for the rest).
- How any of it looks to a person (the evidence pictures are for the mend, not a judgement of the page).
